text:
ashwin: Opening a support case for a brand-new customer account (acct: 210987654321) — we need EC2/GPU soft limit increases in ap-northeast-1 for p5/p4d/g5 and higher ENI/vCPU headroom. Creating the AWS ticket now.

olivia: Please paste the AWS case # and the exact instance counts we requested.

ashwin: Case created: 987654321098765. Summary: "EC2 quota increases for GPU families (p5/p4d/g5) and ENI/vCPU increases for tenant onboarding in ap-northeast-1". Requested initially:
- p5.48xlarge: 6
- p4d.24xlarge: 3
- g5.48xlarge: 8
- vCPU soft limit to 600
- ENI quota to 1500
- EIP soft-limit to 60

sam_infra: Quick CLI checks I ran for the account to attach to the case (saves AWS time):
```
aws ec2 describe-instance-type-offerings --region ap-northeast-1 --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p5.48xlarge,p4d.24xlarge,g5.48xlarge
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-1216C47A
aws service-quotas get-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-A4707A72
``` 

jae: Do we need AZ-level splits? Sometimes they want that for placement and CRs.

ashwin: I specified tokyo-a: 50%, tokyo-b: 30%, tokyo-c: 20%. Also noted we're willing to accept cross-AZ placement and that we can fall back to ap-northeast-2 for p5 if capacity is constrained.

olivia: Add the business justification in the case (expected monthly GPU hours, production inference for customer Y, commit to reserved capacity if needed). Also ping the TAM.

ashwin: Done. Justification: "Production LLM inference (latency + batch), expected ramp to ~45k GPU hours/month by month 2, will consider reserved instances or savings plans for steady state." Cost center: infra-prod-103. TAM: suresh (aws-tam) has been CC'd.

infra-bot: @ashwin created support case 987654321098765. Status: opened.

sam_infra: One note — ap-northeast-1 has historically spotty p5 inventory. Recommend asking for parallel g5 capacity and a placement strategy (model shards across families).

ashwin: Added fallback policy to the case: prefer p5, fall back to g5 for certain replica types, use p4d only for large dense models. Also uploaded a model-to-instance mapping chart.

jae: Also confirm AMI ENA/ENA default drivers and whether ENI counts include secondary IPs per ENI. AWS sometimes counts differently.

ashwin: Confirmed AMIs are ENA-enabled. Clarified ENI count request to cover secondary IPs and container density (stated expected pods per host).

olivia: Any network/NAT/GW throughput asks? Those can be separate quota cases but mention them.

ashwin: Requested NAT Gateway throughput review in the case and asked to bump SG rules to 3500. Also asked for Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) eligibility check for p4d.

infra-bot: Support case 987654321098765 updated by ashwin. Status: initial review by AWS.

ashwin: AWS replied asking for peak concurrent slots and whether we can accept cross-region fallback for p5. They flagged p5 capacity in ap-northeast-1 as constrained.

sam_infra: I pasted concurrency numbers: small replicas ~30 p5-equivalent slots, large replicas ~12 p4d-equivalent slots, batch workers ~200 g5 GPU-hours/day. Pasted in case.

ashwin: Also uploaded a PO/customer contract copy to speed approval. AWS requested a TAM confirm — suresh confirmed in the case and escalated to their account team.

olivia: Good. Timeline expectation? With TAM it should be 48-96 hours typically.

jae: If AWS cannot approve p5 in ap-northeast-1, ask for temporary CR for p5 in ap-northeast-2 or reserved capacity in another region as a stopgap.

ashwin: Noted. AWS moved the case to provisioning and created internal change request CR-888777 for this account. They provisioned g5 and p4d temporarily: approved g5.48xlarge = 8 (as requested), p4d.24xlarge = 3 (as requested). p5 family remains pending due to regional capacity.

infra-bot: Support case 987654321098765 status: provisioning (CR-888777 created).

olivia: Please add an onboarding checklist item to track the p5 follow-up and CR number.

ashwin: Added board ticket ONB-8023 linking to case 987654321098765 and CR-888777.

sam_infra: AWS updated: they can approve a limited p5 allocation — p5.48xlarge = 3 in ap-northeast-1 with option to request scale-up in 21 days; they recommended cross-region fallback for peak spikes. They've set the ENI/vCPU/EIP limits to requested values now.

ashwin: Uploaded the final accepted counts and notified the customer. AWS closed the case with notes on scale-up procedure and contact points. Final case status: resolved.

infra-bot: Case 987654321098765 status: resolved (limits updated).
